newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on correction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Monday due to a technical correction after Friday's sharp falls, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 21,080 yuan ($2,539) per tonne, rising 80 yuan. It opened at 21,000 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,950 and a high of 21,180.
December rose 130 to 20,770, January 170 to 21,070, March 100 to 21,080, April 80 to 21,050 and May fell 20 to 21,010.
Combined volume fell to 50,990 tonnes from 69,860.
Copper opened little changed from Friday's close, then speculative buying and selling pushed copper up and down at high levels, trader said.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines, with the short-term market trend unclear.
"Despite Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange, today's trend was a technical correction," one trader said.
"But thin volume indicated the confidence of long position holders was not as strong as in the past few days," he added.
Traders attributed this to a rise in LME stockpiles.
"Some investors doubt whether LME stockpiles will continue to fall," a second trader said. "That is why investors did not want to buy today."
Analysts expect copper to consolidate at current levels in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. December fell 60 to 13,850 yuan per tonne and January was down 100 to 14,050.
Combined volume fell to 250 tonnes from 850.
